cases.preference_reason: The revision removes three local sources of backtracking without changing practical advice. The original was already technically sound; this is a clarity improvement, not a demonstrated user-outcome improvement.

reconstruction.conclusion: Disabling in-progress cancellation does not ensure every waiting run survives.
reconstruction.next_action: Keep cancel-in-progress: false and set queue: max when several runs should wait.
reconstruction.limiting_condition: The contention is within the same repository and group; capacity is 100 pending runs, excess arrivals are canceled, and retained runs follow entry into waiting rather than dispatch order.

qualifiers_verified: Same group and same repository govern contention.
queue: single remains explicitly the default and replacement applies to the pending run.
queue: max retains up to 100 pending runs; arrivals beyond capacity are canceled.
The ordering claim names retained runs and distinguishes waiting time from dispatch time.
false is a compatible configuration choice, without claiming it must be explicitly written.
queue: max with cancel-in-progress: true fails validation.
Active-run cancellation with true remains limited to the default-queue discussion.
Protects active work is read in the stated concurrency-setting context, not as immunity from unrelated cancellation.

cases.source_verification: Live GitHub.com property definitions and queue example confirm single/max capacity, overflow cancellation, incompatibility with true, repository scope and FIFO by waiting time. Some generic examples omit cancellation conditions; the normative property definitions control this review.

original_assessment.correctness: Supported by the official TaskGroup and task-cancellation documentation.
original_assessment.relevance: Covers sibling cancellation, caller-visible grouped failures, cleanup, cancellation propagation and the minimum version.
original_assessment.clarity: Readable, but This happens leaves the wait-before-report relationship indirect; the cancellation exception and version requirement appear later than their governing claim.
original_assessment.qualifier_completeness: The necessary ordinary-exception, child-cancellation and special-base-exception qualifications are present.

revision_assessment.correctness: All nine supplied claims retain their meaning; no factual correction or unsupported addition was found.
revision_assessment.relevance: Retains the complete answer to the worker-failure question.
revision_assessment.clarity: The minimum version is immediately visible, child cancellation is distinguished beside the sibling-cancellation trigger, and exception-group timing is named explicitly.
revision_assessment.tone: Maintains the original's direct register and the qualified cleanup recommendation.
revision_assessment.qualifier_completeness: Generally, alone, ordinary exceptions, wait-before-raise, and the special KeyboardInterrupt/SystemExit path all remain.

cases.preference_reason: The revision makes the prerequisite and causal timing easier to locate without changing the cleanup paragraph or increasing certainty. The opening paragraph is denser, but its statements are now in a useful dependency order.

reconstruction.conclusion: On Python 3.11 or later, an ordinary child failure cancels siblings; the group waits for children before raising their non-cancellation failures together.
reconstruction.next_action: Use TaskGroup for the batch, put child cleanup in try/finally, and generally re-raise explicitly caught CancelledError after cleanup.
reconstruction.limiting_condition: A child's CancelledError alone does not trigger sibling cancellation; the group type depends on collected failures, KeyboardInterrupt/SystemExit are re-raised specially, and failure closes the group to new tasks.

qualifiers_verified: Ordinary exceptions such as ValueError cause sibling cancellation.
A child's CancelledError alone does not cause sibling cancellation; this does not rule out external group cancellation.
ExceptionGroup is conditional on all collected failures being ordinary exceptions.
The group waits for every child before raising collected failures; the wait does not postpone the cancellation request.
Cancellation is raised at the next opportunity and cleanup belongs inside child coroutines.
Generally re-raise remains qualified, and the warning says swallowing can interfere rather than asserting inevitable failure.
BaseExceptionGroup remains available when required by collected failures.
KeyboardInterrupt and SystemExit retain cancel-then-wait-then-re-raise behavior.
The first non-cancellation failure prevents new tasks; Python 3.11 or later remains the minimum version.

cases.source_verification: Live Python 3.14.7 documentation confirms the described child-failure, cleanup and exception-reporting behavior, and records TaskGroup as added in Python 3.11. No runtime test was performed.

limitations: Both questions and originals are synthetic; this comparison does not establish performance on naturally occurring discussions.
Preference is an LLM editorial judgment, not a human preference measurement.
